content:
# Judith Chapter 4 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## Summary
Total disagreements: 13

---

## Disagreement 1 — Verse 4:1: Report structure

**EMET:** "heard all that Holofernes... had-done to-the nations, and how he-had-plundered all their temples."
**LOGOS:** "heard everything that Holofernes... had done to the nations, and how he had plundered all their temples."
**PNEUMA:** "heard what Holofernes had been doing — every temple looted, every nation handed over for destruction." (Inverts and condenses the list.)
**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS. The two-part structure (what he did to nations + specifically plundering temples) is important. PNEUMA's inversion loses the narrative sequence and adds "in full" without warrant.

---

## Disagreement 2 — Verse 4:2: Degree of fear

**EMET:** "they-were-greatly-afraid before his face and they-trembled for Jerusalem."
**LOGOS:** "They were greatly afraid before him and trembled for Jerusalem."
**PNEUMA:** "They were terrified. Not just afraid — genuinely terrified." (Rhetorical repetition; paragraph break.)
**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS. The Greek ἐφοβήθησαν σφόδρα is "they feared greatly" — strong but not deserving the dramatic repetition PNEUMA adds. LOGOS's simple rendering is accurate.

---

## Disagreement 3 — Verse 4:3: Temple rededication

**EMET:** "the-vessels and the-altar and the-house [had been consecrated] after the-pollution."
**LOGOS:** "the vessels and the altar and the house had just been reconsecrated after their defilement."
**PNEUMA:** "The sacred vessels, the altar, the temple itself had only recently been rededicated after the defilement."
**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS. "Reconsecrated after their defilement" — the Greek μολυσμόν = defilement/pollution. LOGOS's "defilement" is more precise than PNEUMA's "the defilement" (loses specific referent). "Sacred vessels" (PNEUMA) adds "sacred" without warrant; the Greek simply has τὰ σκεύη.

---

## Disagreement 4 — Verse 4:4: Extent of communication

**EMET:** Preserves the full geographical list: Samaria, Kona, Beth-horon, Belmain, Jericho, Choba, Aesora, valley of Salem.
**LOGOS/PNEUMA:** Both preserve the list but vary connective tissue.
**PNEUMA:** Adds "urgent word" for ἀπέστειλαν (they sent).
**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS. The Greek simply says "they sent" — "urgent" is an addition. The full geographical list is preserved by all three; LOGOS's connective structure is natural.

---

## Disagreement 5 — Verse 4:5: Pre-emptive military action

**EMET:** "they-seized-beforehand all-the heights of-the high mountains and they-fortified the-villages that-were in them and they-stored-up provisions for-the preparation of war."
**LOGOS:** "They seized the heights of the high mountains in advance, fortified the villages in them, and stored up provisions in preparation for war."
**PNEUMA:** "They moved fast. They seized the mountain heights, fortified the hilltop villages, and stockpiled provisions for war."
**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS. "In advance" appropriately renders the Greek προκατελάβοντο (pre-emptive seizure). "Stored up provisions" is more precise than "stockpiled." PNEUMA adds "They moved fast" without warrant.

---

## Disagreement 6 — Verse 4:6: High priest's identity and authority

**EMET:** "Joakim the-high priest, who-was in Jerusalem in those days, wrote to-the ones dwelling in Bethulia and Betomesthaim."
**LOGOS:** "Joakim the high priest, who was in Jerusalem at that time, wrote to those dwelling in Bethulia and Betomesthaim."
**PNEUMA:** "Joakim the high priest, directing affairs from Jerusalem, sent orders to the towns of Bethulia and Betomesthaim."
**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS. "Directing affairs from Jerusalem" (PNEUMA) is an interpretive addition. The Greek ἔγραψεν simply means "he wrote" — letters, not oral orders. PNEUMA's "sent orders" also loses the written medium.

---

## Disagreement 7 — Verse 4:7: The mountain passes

**EMET:** "commanding them to-seize-in-advance the-ascents of-the hill-country, because through them was the-entrance into Judea, and it-was easy to-prevent those-advancing, because the-approach was narrow, [allowing] only two men [to pass] together."
**LOGOS:** "ordering them to seize the passes through the hill country in advance, since these were the gateways into Judea and it would be easy to hold off those advancing — the approach was so narrow that only two men could pass through together."
**PNEUMA:** "telling them to hold the mountain passes at all costs. These passes were the doorways into Judea. The terrain made them defensible: the approach was so narrow that only two men could walk abreast."
**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS. "Gateways" for εἴσοδοι is accurate. "Hold off those advancing" for κωλῦσαι τοὺς ἀναβαίνοντας is precise. PNEUMA's "at all costs" adds urgency not in the Greek. "Walk abreast" is a good rendering of κατὰ δύο ἄνδρας ὁμοῦ but LOGOS's "pass through together" is equally valid.

---

## Disagreement 8 — Verse 4:8: Council authority

**EMET:** "as-had-been-commanded [to] them by Joakim the-high priest and the-council of-all-the people of Israel."
**LOGOS:** "as Joakim the high priest and the council of all the people of Israel assembled in Jerusalem had commanded them."
**PNEUMA:** "every order from Joakim and the council of the people assembled in Jerusalem."
**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS. The full title "council of all the people of Israel" should be preserved — it establishes the communal authority structure. PNEUMA's abbreviation to "the council of the people" loses "all" (πάντος).

---

## Disagreement 9 — Verse 4:9: "humbled their souls" vs. "humbled themselves"

**EMET:** "they-humbled their-souls with great earnestness."
**LOGOS:** "they humbled themselves before him with great earnestness."
**PNEUMA:** "They humbled themselves before him with everything they had."
**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS. The Greek ἐταπείνωσαν τὰς ψυχὰς αὐτῶν = "they humbled their souls" — a significant phrase echoing the Yom Kippur fasting language. EMET preserves "souls" which is the precise object. LOGOS's "themselves" is natural. PNEUMA's "with everything they had" is an expansion.

---

## Disagreement 10 — Verse 4:10: Scope of mourners

**EMET:** "They and their-wives and their-children and their-cattle and every-sojourner and hired-servant and slave bought-with-their-money — they-girded sackcloth upon their-loins."
**LOGOS:** "They — along with their wives and their children and their cattle and every resident alien and hired worker and slave purchased with their money — girded sackcloth on their loins."
**PNEUMA:** "men, women, children, livestock, resident aliens, hired workers, even the household slaves. All of them put on sackcloth."
**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS. The bracketed em-dash construction renders the Greek list structure well. "Every resident alien" for πάντα πάροικον is the standard term. PNEUMA loses "purchased with their money" (ἠγορασμένον ἀργυρίου) which specifies the legal status of these slaves.

---

## Disagreement 11 — Verse 4:12: Prayer content

**EMET:** "not to-give their-infants into plunder and their wives into spoil and the-cities of their-inheritance into destruction and the-sanctuary into desecration and disgrace, as-a reproach to-the nations."
**LOGOS:** "not to give their infants as plunder and their wives as spoil and the cities of their inheritance to destruction and the sanctuary to desecration and disgrace — not to make it a reproach among the nations."
**PNEUMA:** "Do not give our children over to plunder. Do not let our wives become war spoil. Do not let the cities we inherited be destroyed. Do not let your sanctuary be desecrated and shamed before the nations." (Switches to direct speech.)
**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS. The prayer is reported speech in the Greek (infinitive clauses), not direct address. PNEUMA's switch to direct second-person address changes the rhetorical register. The fourfold structure of what they prayed against should be preserved. "Infants" (νήπια) is more precise than PNEUMA's "children."

---

## Disagreement 12 — Verse 4:14: Temple sacrifices terminology

**EMET:** "the-continual-offering and the-vow-offerings and the-freewill-offerings."
**LOGOS:** "the daily burnt offering and the votive offerings and the freewill offerings."
**PNEUMA:** "the daily sacrifices, the votive offerings, and the freewill gifts of the people."
**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS. "Daily burnt offering" for ὁλοκαύτωμα ἐνδελεχισμοῦ is technically accurate — the tamid offering. "Votive offerings" for εὐχάς and "freewill offerings" for ἑκουσίους are standard. PNEUMA's "freewill gifts" softens the cultic specificity.

---

## Disagreement 13 — Verse 4:15: Final petition

**EMET:** "so-that he-might look with-good-favor upon all-the house of Israel."
**LOGOS:** "asking that he look with favor on the whole house of Israel."
**PNEUMA:** "look with favor on us. Save the whole house of Israel." (Adds "Save" without Greek basis.)
**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS. "Look with favor" for ἐπιβλέψαι is accurate. PNEUMA adds "Save the whole house of Israel" which is an interpretive expansion — the Greek only has the single petition for favorable regard. "Whole house" for πᾶν τὸν οἶκον is preserved.
